events.title: US reopens border to Mexican cattle imports after screwworm-related suspension
events.why: The reopening lets Mexico resume live cattle exports to the US after two suspension periods tied to a screwworm outbreak had cut shipments and pushed up US beef prices.

coverage.title: US reopens border to Mexican cattle imports after screwworm-related suspension
coverage.summary: The reopening lets Mexico resume live cattle exports to the US after two suspension periods tied to a screwworm outbreak had cut shipments and pushed up US beef prices.

coverage.title: United States reopens border to Mexican cattle imports after year-long ban
coverage.summary: The US had blocked Mexican cattle for more than a year to contain rising beef prices for American consumers. The reopening is meant to ease pressure on meat costs while keeping monitoring in place.

events.background: Mexico suspended live cattle shipments to the United States twice after a screwworm outbreak, a parasite that infests livestock and can spread quickly once it crosses the border.
events.view: The reopening restores a trade channel that had been shut for animal health reasons rather than economic ones, so ranchers regain access to the US market they had before the outbreak. The arrangement now depends on Mexico controlling the parasite, not on any shift in US demand for beef.
events.prediction: Cattle shipments are likely to resume and continue without interruption. That would be proven wrong if new screwworm cases are detected and the United States closes the border again.

events.title: Zacatecas violence threatens Morena's hold on the state ahead of 2027 vote
events.why: The killings mix drug trafficking cells, economic interests and political fragility in a state governed by the ruling party, raising doubts about Morena's position heading into the 2027 succession.

coverage.title: Zacatecas violence threatens Morena's hold on the state ahead of 2027 vote
coverage.summary: The killings mix drug trafficking cells, economic interests and political fragility in a state governed by the ruling party, raising doubts about Morena's position heading into the 2027 succession.

events.background: Zacatecas is governed by Morena, and the state faces a gubernatorial succession vote in 2027. The federal government has reported homicides down nationally, but INEGI's victimization survey found 93.2% of crimes nationwide are never reported or investigated, so local violence can spike without changing that national count.
events.view: A multiple homicide involving a former mayor and local officials points to organized crime embedded in local governance, not just street-level extortion. That undercuts the ruling party's national security narrative in a state it needs to hold in 2027, because voters judge safety locally, not by federal statistics. The mechanism is criminal groups competing for control of local economic and political posts, which national homicide trends do not capture.
events.prediction: Morena will likely try to contain the story as an isolated criminal matter rather than a systemic failure, and campaign for 2027 on the national homicide decline. That view fails if further high-profile killings hit Zacatecas officials before the election or if investigators tie the attack directly to sitting local government figures.

coverage.title: Sheinbaum, tras su reunión con Greer: “Avanzamos en la revisión del TMEC y en acuerdos bilaterales”
coverage.summary: El encuentro entre los gobiernos de México y EE UU forma parte de la primera revisión anual del tratado, después de la negativa de Trump de extenderlo por 16 años

events.background: Under Article 34.7 of the trade agreement, the United States, Mexico and Canada must hold a joint review since Washington declined the option of a 16-year extension on 1 July 2026, and the countries now review the pact annually rather than renegotiating it outright.
events.drivers: Talks focused on steel, aluminum and derivative products, regional value chains, and reducing reliance on Asian imports, led by Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard and USTR Jamieson Greer.
events.next: The two governments will hold a fourth round of talks in the first half of September to continue the joint review.
events.view: A third round ending in another meeting date, rather than a text or a decision, shows the review is still at the technical-talks stage, not the negotiating stage. Steel, aluminum and Chinese-content rules are being discussed, but nothing here changes rules of origin or tariffs for a single exporter yet. The benefit for now goes to officials who can point to "constructive" progress without committing either government to a position.
events.prediction: The fourth round in September most likely produces further technical alignment rather than a signed change to the agreement's terms. That expectation would be wrong if the September meeting instead produces a joint statement on specific rule changes, such as new steel or automotive content thresholds.

events.title: Mexico loses more than 500,000 industrial jobs in June
events.why: The services sector also reported sharp job losses despite the World Cup, adding to signs of a weakening labor market this year.

coverage.title: Mexico loses more than 500,000 industrial jobs in June
coverage.summary: The services sector also reported sharp job losses despite the World Cup, adding to signs of a weakening labor market this year.

events.background: Mexico's National Occupation and Employment Survey (ENOE), run by INEGI, tracks month-to-month changes in formal and informal employment across sectors including manufacturing, construction, mining and services.
events.view: A monthly drop of 611,978 industrial jobs, with manufacturing accounting for 482,652 of that and construction another 120,877, is a sharp reversal for an economy already growing near 0.6% in 2025 with fixed investment falling from 23.8% to 22.4% of GDP. The construction losses matter most for nearshoring claims, because physical construction, not investment announcements, is the actual evidence that new plants are being built. Services losing 597,891 jobs the same month, despite World Cup-driven demand, suggests the weakness is broad rather than sector-specific.
events.prediction: Further ENOE readings are likely to show continued softness in manufacturing and construction employment unless fixed investment as a share of GDP stops declining. That view would be wrong if the next ENOE release shows industrial employment rebounding without a matching jump in fixed investment or grid connections.

events.title: BYD to deploy ultra-fast EV chargers across Mexico
events.why: The Chinese automaker plans a network of 100 fast chargers capable of recovering 10% to 70% battery in five minutes, preparing the market for its electric vehicle lineup.

coverage.title: BYD to deploy ultra-fast EV chargers across Mexico
coverage.summary: The Chinese automaker plans a network of 100 fast chargers capable of recovering 10% to 70% battery in five minutes, preparing the market for its electric vehicle lineup.

events.background: BYD is a Chinese automaker expanding into Mexico's electric vehicle market, where charging infrastructure is scarce and adoption is still limited compared with combustion vehicles.
events.view: A planned 100-charger network is an announcement of intended deployment, not yet construction or operation. Fast chargers restoring 10% to 70% of a battery in five minutes would address a real barrier to EV adoption, but the number has no stated comparison to Mexico's existing charger count or geographic coverage, so its scale cannot be judged from what is given. The rollout would primarily support demand for BYD's own vehicle lineup.
events.prediction: Charger construction will probably follow BYD's sales expansion rather than arrive as one nationwide buildout. If specific sites, grid connection dates, or installed charger counts are confirmed, the plan has moved beyond an announcement.

events.title: Sheinbaum responds to new US tariffs, seeks end to trade surprises
events.why: The president acknowledged the difficulty of negotiating with Washington's protectionist turn and said Mexico wants regional rules of origin that benefit the country as the tariff review continues.

coverage.title: Sheinbaum responds to new US tariffs, seeks end to trade surprises
coverage.summary: The president acknowledged the difficulty of negotiating with Washington's protectionist turn and said Mexico wants regional rules of origin that benefit the country as the tariff review continues.

events.background: Since the United States declined to extend the USMCA treaty at the July 2026 review, the three countries now conduct annual reviews, and exports that fail to meet regional rules of origin do not qualify for tariff-free treatment under the pact.
events.view: The new 10% US tariff applies only to Mexican exports that fall outside USMCA rules of origin, so Sheinbaum's push is really about tightening or clarifying those origin rules to keep more exports classified as compliant. This matters because Mexico imports far more from China than it exports there, and origin rules are aimed at Chinese content moving through Mexican factories. The benefit of a clearer rule falls to exporters who can prove regional content, not to those relying on Chinese inputs.
events.prediction: Mexico will likely keep negotiating narrower carve-outs rather than accept a blanket tariff, given it already avoided the higher universal rate applied to over 60 other economies. That view fails if Washington applies new tariffs to USMCA-compliant goods as well, not just non-compliant ones.

events.prediction: Killings of local officials are likely to continue at a similar pace without a targeted change in strategy toward municipal capture. That would be disproven if the annual count drops well below the 2025 pace.

events.title: Moody's warns on falling federal transfers to states as welfare spending rises
events.why: Federal revenue shared with states grew just 0.9% annually between January and May, even as scholarship and pension programs squeeze the finance ministry's budget.

coverage.title: Moody's warns on falling federal transfers to states as welfare spending rises
coverage.summary: Federal revenue shared with states grew just 0.9% annually between January and May, even as scholarship and pension programs squeeze the finance ministry's budget.

events.background: States depend on participaciones federales, a share of federal tax revenue distributed under a formula tied to overall collection (the Recaudación Federal Participable), for a large part of their budgets.
events.drivers: Moody's Local points to slowing national growth and the resulting slowdown in RFP collection, while spending on social transfers keeps rising and squeezing Hacienda's operating budget.
events.implications: Moody's says the mismatch between slowing revenue and rising operating spending could shrink operating margins for states and municipalities by the end of 2026.
events.view: Federal revenue sharing grew just 0.9% annually from January to May while national scholarship and pension spending keeps rising, so the federal government is protecting welfare transfers at the expense of the pool that funds states. Twenty-three of Mexico's states saw their federal transfers fall in the first half of the year against only nine that saw gains, meaning most states face tighter budgets while national welfare programs are shielded.
events.prediction: State governments will likely cut discretionary spending or delay projects in the second half of 2026 unless federal tax collection accelerates. That view is wrong if the Recaudación Federal Participable growth rate rises well above 0.9% and reverses the decline for most states.

events.title: CFE and Cubico sign $1 billion renewable energy joint venture
events.why: Mexico's state power company and Cubico plan to build 578 megawatts of renewable capacity and 500 megawatt-hours of battery storage across four regions.

coverage.title: CFE and Cubico sign $1 billion renewable energy joint venture
coverage.summary: Mexico's state power company and Cubico plan to build 578 megawatts of renewable capacity and 500 megawatt-hours of battery storage across four regions.

coverage.title: Cubico and CFE sign partnership for 578 MW of projects
coverage.summary: Cubico says the five projects include 578 MW of generation and 175.7 MW of batteries storing 500 MWh. Construction of the 78 MW Altamira solar plant is scheduled for December 2026, with the other four projects scheduled for the second quarter of 2027.

coverage.title: Cubico and CFE partner on 500 MWh of battery storage in Mexico
coverage.summary: CFE selected 37 renewable projects totaling 7,411 MW under the mixed investment model, making Cubico's 578 MW portfolio 7.8% of the awarded capacity. CFE must retain at least 54% of each project company, while Cubico provides equity and manages development and construction.

events.drivers: The joint venture targets nearshoring-driven power demand in Tamaulipas, Nuevo León, Campeche and the Yucatán Peninsula.
events.implications: The 25-year partnership signals a structured path for private capital investment aligned with state-led planning rather than fully private generation.
events.background: The $1 billion is planned investment across five projects. None is under construction yet. Under the mixed investment model, the state utility must own at least 54% of each project company. Cubico supplies the equity and manages development and construction, while the state utility may contribute land, permits, studies and long-term purchase agreements.
events.view: This is a test of whether Mexico can bring private capital back into electricity while the state utility keeps control. Cubico's 578 MW is 7.8% of the first 7,411 MW awarded under the model, large enough to test it across four regions but nowhere near enough to settle Mexico's need for new power. If majority state ownership and long-term purchase agreements make the projects financeable, the structure can be repeated with other developers.
events.prediction: The 78 MW Altamira solar plant should reach construction first, in December, while the other four projects move more slowly. If all four begin construction in the second quarter of 2027 as planned, the schedule is holding better than expected. Meeting both dates and repeating the structure in later awards would be the first evidence that the model can scale.

events.title: US and Mexican treasuries sanction Jalisco cartel's financial network
events.why: The action targets more than 50 people and companies tied to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, including the stepson of its leader known as 'El Mencho,' marking one of the largest joint financial strikes against the group.

coverage.title: US and Mexican treasuries sanction Jalisco cartel's financial network
coverage.summary: The action targets more than 50 people and companies tied to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, including the stepson of its leader known as 'El Mencho,' marking one of the largest joint financial strikes against the group.

coverage.title: US and Mexico sanction financial network tied to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel
coverage.summary: Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit and the US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control targeted people and companies linked to the cartel, including its reported new leader, as authorities pursue the group's finances.

events.background: The US designation freezes property under US jurisdiction and blocks transactions with listed people and companies. Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit also filed a money-laundering complaint, but prosecutors and courts must turn that intelligence into charges or seizures.
events.drivers: Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit filed a complaint with the federal attorney general's office alleging money laundering tied to the sanctioned network, while the US Treasury froze the assets of those listed.
events.implications: The sanctions cut off a network of individuals and companies accused of financing the cartel through money laundering.
events.next: Mexico's Attorney General's office will pursue prosecution of the sanctioned individuals following the Financial Intelligence Unit's complaint.
events.view: More than 50 people and companies sounds broad, but designations are not the same as prosecutions or seized assets. The joint action gives Mexico and the US a shared map of the network. It changes the cartel's operating costs only if Mexican investigators use that map to freeze accounts, seize property and bring cases.
events.prediction: The designations are more likely to freeze assets than produce immediate criminal cases in Mexico. If prosecutors file charges, courts order seizures, or listed companies are removed from the network, the operation is reaching Mexico's criminal and corporate systems. Those outcomes, not the length of the sanctions list, will show whether the joint operation changed how the cartel moves money.

events.title: Mexico's economic activity falls in May, ending three-month growth streak
events.why: The statistics agency's monthly indicator shows a contraction after three months of gains, though the January-May period still posts 1.1% annual growth.

coverage.title: Mexico's economic activity falls in May, ending three-month growth streak
coverage.summary: The statistics agency's monthly indicator shows a contraction after three months of gains, though the January-May period still posts 1.1% annual growth.

events.background: Mexico's statistics agency publishes the Global Indicator of Economic Activity, a monthly measure of output that arrives before quarterly GDP. It separates farming, industry and services, which helps show whether a national move is broad or concentrated.
events.drivers: Industrial activity fell 0.8% and farm output fell 0.5% month on month in May, while services grew 0.2%, driving the overall monthly contraction.
events.implications: Monex says future growth will keep depending on the strength of an industrial recovery, domestic demand, and uncertainty from tariffs and the USMCA review.
events.next: Monex expects the economy to show improvement in June as the industrial sector recovers and services maintain a steady pace.
events.view: May's decline is not large enough on its own to call a downturn. The useful split is underneath it: industry fell 0.8%, farming fell 0.5%, and services rose 0.2%. That means services are carrying growth and makes an industrial rebound, not the headline total, the clearest test of whether the first-quarter slowdown is ending.
events.prediction: A weak June is more likely than a clean rebound, with services still doing more of the work than industry. If industry returns to growth while services remain positive, May will look more like a temporary setback. Another industrial decline would make the slowdown look broader and harder to dismiss as one bad month.

coverage.title: USTR recommends tighter USMCA auto rules of origin
coverage.summary: The trade office cites a shrinking US content share in vehicles assembled in Mexico and Canada and regional reliance on chips and circuit boards sourced outside North America.

events.background: USMCA rules of origin set the regional content vehicles need to qualify for tariff-free treatment, and the pact now undergoes annual reviews after Washington declined a 16-year extension.
events.drivers: USTR points to a shrinking US content share in vehicles built in Mexico and Canada and to regional reliance on chips, circuit boards and display panels from non-market economies.
events.implications: Mexico faces 25% duties on vehicles and parts that fail to meet the qualifying content threshold.

events.title: Forced-labor complaint over Chinese camera imports tests USMCA mechanism
events.why: Civil groups file what they call the first citizen-driven case under the trade pact, accusing Mexico of allowing imports linked to forced labor, a claim that could trigger formal review procedures with the US.

coverage.title: Forced-labor complaint over Chinese camera imports tests USMCA mechanism
coverage.summary: Civil groups file what they call the first citizen-driven case under the trade pact, accusing Mexico of allowing imports linked to forced labor, a claim that could trigger formal review procedures with the US.

events.background: Article 23.6 of USMCA lets citizens file complaints over forced-labor imports, and the US has proposed a 10% minimum tariff for most partners on goods linked to forced labor.
events.drivers: Civil groups ProDESC and Empower revived a complaint over Dahua and Hikvision surveillance cameras tied to Xinjiang supply chains, filed with the labor ministry in 2023 and dismissed that same year.
events.implications: The case adds to US scrutiny of Mexico during the T-MEC review at the same time Mexico is trying to avoid the proposed 10% forced-labor tariff.

events.title: Chedraui profit falls 11.5% on US immigration crackdown
events.why: The retailer says fewer Hispanic shoppers visited its US supermarkets as immigration enforcement intensified, compounded by exchange-rate pressure on its earnings.

coverage.title: Chedraui profit falls 11.5% on US immigration crackdown
coverage.summary: The retailer says fewer Hispanic shoppers visited its US supermarkets as immigration enforcement intensified, compounded by exchange-rate pressure on its earnings.

events.background: Chedraui operates supermarkets serving Hispanic communities in the United States, exposing its US business to shifts in immigration enforcement and to swings in the peso-dollar exchange rate.

events.title: Walmart to cut Mexico workweek to 40 hours starting 2027
events.why: The move follows a legal requirement for Mexican companies to reduce standard hours from 48 to 40, with a phase-in period beginning this year.

coverage.title: Walmart to cut Mexico workweek to 40 hours starting 2027
coverage.summary: The move follows a legal requirement for Mexican companies to reduce standard hours from 48 to 40, with a phase-in period beginning this year.

events.background: Mexican labor law currently sets a standard 48-hour workweek, and a reform pushed by the Sheinbaum government requires companies to cut it to 40 hours in stages between 2027 and 2030.
events.drivers: The labor ministry set 2026 as the year for companies to adjust their operations, and Walmart says it tested different operating models and productivity initiatives before committing to the January 2027 start.
events.implications: An EY report found 72% of companies in the Mexican market have not yet taken specific steps to adapt to the shorter workweek.
events.next: The reduction will phase in gradually by two hours a year until reaching 40 hours in 2030.

events.title: AT&T Mexico loses 668,000 prepaid users under phone registry rule
events.why: A new requirement linking mobile lines to user identity cut into AT&T's prepaid base, though postpaid growth kept revenue and cash flow rising.

coverage.title: AT&T Mexico loses 668,000 prepaid users under phone registry rule
coverage.summary: A new requirement linking mobile lines to user identity cut into AT&T's prepaid base, though postpaid growth kept revenue and cash flow rising.

events.background: Mexico's telecom regulator requires prepaid mobile lines to be registered to a verified identity, a rule meant to curb crime linked to anonymous phone use.

events.title: Mexico files 20 legal complaints over deaths of nationals in ICE custody
events.why: The foreign ministry expands a legal offensive announced two weeks ago after 17 Mexicans died in US custody, with eight complaints directed at state prosecutors.

coverage.title: Mexico files 20 legal complaints over deaths of nationals in ICE custody
coverage.summary: The foreign ministry expands a legal offensive announced two weeks ago after 17 Mexicans died in US custody, with eight complaints directed at state prosecutors.

events.background: Mexico's Foreign Ministry (SRE) has pursued a legal campaign since July 9 over the deaths of at least 17 Mexican nationals in US custody or during ICE operations since May 2025.
events.drivers: The ministry has now filed 20 criminal complaints in the United States, eight with state prosecutors and twelve with county prosecutors, expanding the earlier announced offensive.
events.next: The content of the complaints has not yet been made public.
events.implications: The federal attorney general's office (FGR) formalized a separate recourse already sent to the US Department of Justice.

events.title: Security chief says Mexico has not located El Mayo's properties
events.why: García Harfuch says it is up to the attorney general's office to decide on an extradition request for the jailed Sinaloa Cartel leader, who wants to serve part of his sentence in Mexico.

coverage.title: Security chief says Mexico has not located El Mayo's properties
coverage.summary: García Harfuch says it is up to the attorney general's office to decide on an extradition request for the jailed Sinaloa Cartel leader, who wants to serve part of his sentence in Mexico.

events.drivers: Zambada's lawyer, Frank Pérez, disclosed that the 76-year-old wants to serve part of his sentence in Mexico, prompting reporters to press Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch on a possible extradition request.
events.implications: García Harfuch says Mexican authorities have seized accounts and properties linked to the Sinaloa Cartel, but none registered under Zambada's name.
events.background: Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada is the former Sinaloa Cartel leader sentenced to life in a US prison for drug trafficking, with a US court also ordering forfeiture of assets tied to the cartel.
events.next: García Harfuch said it is the federal attorney general's office, the FGR, that would have to decide whether to request Zambada's extradition.

events.title: Sheinbaum takes cautious stance on possible new US tariffs against 60 countries
events.why: The economy ministry says it presented arguments to US officials for why Mexico should be excluded from any new round of tariffs.

coverage.title: Sheinbaum takes cautious stance on possible new US tariffs against 60 countries
coverage.summary: The economy ministry says it presented arguments to US officials for why Mexico should be excluded from any new round of tariffs.

events.background: The caution comes amid USMCA's ongoing annual review and after USTR Jamieson Greer said new Section 301 tariffs would target countries where goods are produced with forced labor.
events.drivers: Mexico's Economy Ministry held a hearing with US officials last week to argue against including Mexico in the new tariffs.
events.next: Sheinbaum said Mexico must wait for an official US government position on which countries are affected.

events.title: US prepares new tariff of up to 10% over forced-labor concerns on coffee and tomatoes
events.why: Washington maintains a block on Mexican companies over forced-labor allegations and is preparing an additional tariff, adding pressure during the USMCA review.

coverage.title: US prepares new tariff of up to 10% over forced-labor concerns on coffee and tomatoes
coverage.summary: Washington maintains a block on Mexican companies over forced-labor allegations and is preparing an additional tariff, adding pressure during the USMCA review.

events.drivers: A USTR report says Mexico has not effectively enforced its own ban on forced-labor imports, letting such goods undercut costs and gain an unfair advantage in the Mexican market.
events.implications: The finding adds pressure on coffee and tomato exporters as Washington prepares a tariff of up to 10% tied to labor compliance.
events.background: US Customs and Border Protection can issue Withhold Release Orders to block goods suspected of being made with forced labor, a tool already used against some Mexican companies under USMCA's labor provisions.

events.title: Volaris-Viva airline merger advances in Colombia, eyes Mexico approval this year
events.why: The merger would create a new holding group, Grupo Más Vuelos, and still needs regulatory clearance in Mexico.

coverage.title: Volaris-Viva airline merger advances in Colombia, eyes Mexico approval this year
coverage.summary: The merger would create a new holding group, Grupo Más Vuelos, and still needs regulatory clearance in Mexico.

events.drivers: Colombia approved the deal in late April, and Volaris has completed two-thirds of the information requests from Mexico's antitrust commission, the CNA.
events.next: The airlines are still supplying information to the US Department of Justice, and Volaris asked Mexico's securities regulator, the CNBV, in May for authorization, with both companies expecting remaining approvals before year end.
events.background: Grupo Más Vuelos would combine Volaris and Viva into a single holding company under a merger announced in December 2025 that requires clearance from multiple national regulators.
events.implications: Volaris' director said the merger will generate value for customers, investors and the industry.

events.title: Mexico and US customs agencies expand real-time data exchange
events.why: The two countries' customs authorities are building systems to share cargo data in real time, aimed at strengthening verification and curbing illicit trade across the border.

coverage.title: Mexico and US customs agencies expand real-time data exchange
coverage.summary: The two countries' customs authorities are building systems to share cargo data in real time, aimed at strengthening verification and curbing illicit trade across the border.

events.drivers: The initiative aims to validate import and export declarations and combat fuel smuggling along the border.
events.background: ANAM is Mexico's customs agency and CBP its US counterpart, and the two already cooperate on border security matters tied to USMCA-era trade.

events.title: Seventh journalist killed in Mexico this year
events.why: Alejandro Leyva had reported death threats to state and federal authorities a year earlier, but no protective measures were taken, underscoring gaps in Mexico's journalist protection mechanisms.

coverage.title: Seventh journalist killed in Mexico this year
coverage.summary: Alejandro Leyva had reported death threats to state and federal authorities a year earlier, but no protective measures were taken, underscoring gaps in Mexico's journalist protection mechanisms.

events.background: Mexico's journalist protection mechanism is meant to respond to threats against reporters, but enforcement gaps have persisted for years.
events.drivers: Leyva had reported death threats to state and federal authorities a year before his killing, and no protective measures were taken.

events.title: Citi survey sees peso weakening toward 17.92 per dollar by year-end
events.why: The forecast ties the currency's expected slide to uncertainty over the USMCA review and anticipated Banxico moves in the second half of the year.
events.background: Banxico targets 3% inflation and sets its policy rate partly to keep Mexican rates above US levels, a differential that supports the peso and that investors watch closely.
events.drivers: Citi's July survey points to depreciation as USMCA negotiations create uncertainty and analysts anticipate shifts in the Banxico-Fed rate gap.
events.implications: The consensus implies the peso would give back part of its 2.86% first-half gain, closing 2026 near 17.92 pesos per dollar versus 17.49 at midyear.

coverage.title: Citi survey sees peso weakening toward 17.92 per dollar by year-end
coverage.summary: The forecast ties the currency's expected slide to uncertainty over the USMCA review and anticipated Banxico moves in the second half of the year.

events.title: Sheinbaum presses USMCA talks with Trump and Carney at World Cup final
events.why: The brief in-person exchange coincided with the opening of a new round of trilateral trade talks in Mexico City on the treaty's review.
events.background: USMCA links Mexico, the US and Canada, and after the first joint review on 1 July 2026 the US declined a 16-year extension, so the pact now faces annual reviews under Article 34.7 through 2036.
events.drivers: Washington's new 50% tariff on Canadian goods, applied even to treaty-compliant products, is pushing Mexico to seek elimination of duties on its own rules-of-origin-compliant exports.
events.next: Sheinbaum was preparing to host USTR Jamieson Greer in Mexico City as the new round of talks opened.
events.implications: The Canadian tariff, applied despite compliance with the treaty, shows Washington willing to tax partner goods even under USMCA rules.

coverage.title: Sheinbaum presses USMCA talks with Trump and Carney at World Cup final
coverage.summary: The brief in-person exchange coincided with the opening of a new round of trilateral trade talks in Mexico City on the treaty's review.

events.title: Officials report Asian imports fell 23.2% after Mexico’s tariffs
events.why: Officials say the drop in imports from Asia strengthens Mexico's position in the USMCA review by showing reduced reliance on non-regional suppliers.
events.background: In December 2025 Mexico imposed tariffs on imports from countries without a free trade agreement, aiming to curb the Chinese-origin components that flow through its factories despite USMCA rules of origin.
events.drivers: Between January and May, imports under those tariff lines from non-FTA countries fell 23.2% year-on-year, with China's drop at 28.4%, Taiwan's at 32.7% and South Korea's at 21.9%.
events.implications: Despite the broad decline, Chinese heavy trucks remain a separate obstacle to Mexico securing exemption from Trump's tariffs.

coverage.title: Officials report Asian imports fell 23.2% after Mexico’s tariffs
coverage.summary: Officials say the drop in imports from Asia strengthens Mexico's position in the USMCA review by showing reduced reliance on non-regional suppliers.

events.title: Mexico is not among the leading destinations for private AI investment
events.why: The US and Canada rank among the top global recipients of private AI investment while Mexico does not appear on the list, despite all three being partners in the same trade pact.
events.background: Mexico, the US and Canada are USMCA partners, and Stanford's AI Index Report 2026 tracks which countries attract private capital for AI development as computing infrastructure needs grow.
events.implications: The index reported 173 data centers in Mexico at the end of 2025, compared with 337 in Canada and 5,427 in the US.
events.next: Watch new data-center projects and Mexico's position in the next AI Index to see whether the gap narrows.
events.drivers: The US led global private AI investment with $285,880 million in 2025, and Canada also ranked among the top five, while Mexico shows only a rise in graduates trained for technology development rather than investment.

coverage.title: Mexico is not among the leading destinations for private AI investment
coverage.summary: The US and Canada rank among the top global recipients of private AI investment while Mexico does not appear on the list, despite all three being partners in the same trade pact.

events.title: Questions surround the death of Juan Jairo Coronilla, the Mexican who was fleeing ICE: ‘He came with his work visa’
events.why: The 28-year-old from Guanajuato worked as a furniture salesman and had a return ticket to Mexico for July 18.

coverage.title: Questions surround the death of Juan Jairo Coronilla, the Mexican who was fleeing ICE: ‘He came with his work visa’
coverage.summary: The 28-year-old from Guanajuato worked as a furniture salesman and had a return ticket to Mexico for July 18.

events.title: US imposes 50% tariff on Canadian imports, straining North American trade pact
events.why: The tariff, applied under Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act, hits Canadian goods even when they meet USMCA content rules, adding pressure to the trilateral review Mexico is also negotiating.

coverage.title: US imposes 50% tariff on Canadian imports, straining North American trade pact
coverage.summary: The tariff, applied under Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act, hits Canadian goods even when they meet USMCA content rules, adding pressure to the trilateral review Mexico is also negotiating.

events.background: Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act lets Washington impose duties even on goods that meet a trade agreement's content rules, and about 85% of Mexico's exports currently enter the US tariff-free under USMCA.
events.drivers: Washington has escalated tariff actions against Canada even where USMCA content rules are met, adding to existing Section 232 duties on steel, aluminum and automotive goods.
events.implications: The move sets a precedent that could be applied to Mexico's own tariff-free access under the same agreement.

events.title: Banxico and CNBV work to manage risks as fintechs convert into banks
events.why: Regulators are responding as fintech firms obtain banking licenses in Mexico, intensifying competition with incumbent lenders.

coverage.title: Banxico and CNBV work to manage risks as fintechs convert into banks
coverage.summary: Regulators are responding as fintech firms obtain banking licenses in Mexico, intensifying competition with incumbent lenders.

events.background: Banxico, the CNBV and the finance ministry jointly authorize fintechs seeking to convert into full banks, a process now underway for several firms.
events.drivers: FinTech México's Felipe Vallejo says a wave of fintechs converting into banks is pushing incumbent banks to move faster and regulators to weigh the risks of more remote, tech-driven competition.
events.implications: Vallejo frames the shift as producing "only good things" through a competitive cycle among banks and authorities.

events.title: Nu begins operating as a bank in Mexico as Banorte welcomes competition
events.why: The Brazilian fintech's move into full banking status intensifies competition in Mexico's banking sector, according to Banorte executives.

coverage.title: Nu begins operating as a bank in Mexico as Banorte welcomes competition
coverage.summary: The Brazilian fintech's move into full banking status intensifies competition in Mexico's banking sector, according to Banorte executives.

events.background: Mexico's banking sector has a bank credit-to-GDP ratio of about 35.5%, low for a large economy, leaving room for fintechs to convert into full banks under multiple-banking licenses.
events.drivers: Nu México just received regulatory approval for a multiple-banking license, joining Plata and Revolut, which already operate as banks, as fintechs push to compete on equal regulatory footing.
events.next: Mercado Pago, Konfío and Bunq are still awaiting approval to convert to full banking licenses.
events.implications: Banorte's director said the entry of newly licensed fintechs increases competition under the same rules as established banks.

events.title: Mexico rules out domestic cyclospora outbreak, coordinates with US on source
events.why: Mexico's health secretary said the country is not experiencing an outbreak but is working with US authorities to trace the source of an infection reaching record levels in the United States.

coverage.title: Mexico rules out domestic cyclospora outbreak, coordinates with US on source
coverage.summary: Mexico's health secretary said the country is not experiencing an outbreak but is working with US authorities to trace the source of an infection reaching record levels in the United States.

events.background: Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite causing cyclosporiasis, an intestinal illness usually linked to contaminated fresh fruit and vegetables.
events.drivers: A record surge of cases in the United States prompted Mexican and US authorities to investigate whether the outbreak's source lies in Mexico, after Mexico confirmed three cases of its own.
events.implications: Health secretary David Kershenobich says the three Mexican cases fall within normal epidemiology and show no evidence tying Mexico to the US outbreak.
events.next: Mexico says it will continue working with US authorities to determine the outbreak's origin.

events.title: Mexico raises 13 concerns in third round of USMCA review talks
events.why: Mexico's economy ministry pressed its list of trade concerns with US Trade Representative officials as the two countries work to preserve tariff advantages ahead of the pact's renewal decision.

coverage.title: Mexico raises 13 concerns in third round of USMCA review talks
coverage.summary: Mexico's economy ministry pressed its list of trade concerns with US Trade Representative officials as the two countries work to preserve tariff advantages ahead of the pact's renewal decision.

coverage.title: Mexico raises 13 concerns as USMCA review talks open in Mexico City
coverage.summary: The Economy Ministry presented 13 issues to the US Trade Representative's office as the first annual USMCA review round began, a formal step that will shape tariffs, auto rules and market access for years.

events.implications: New US tariffs announced against Canada, the third USMCA partner, have sharpened Mexico's focus on getting tariffs removed among the three member countries.
events.background: The USMCA review is proceeding in rounds, with Washington's USTR pushing to tighten automotive rules of origin and extend them to other products to cut its trade deficit.
events.next: Mexico said it will press the Trump administration to eliminate tariffs among the three member countries.
events.drivers: Mexico's Economy Ministry, led by Ebrard, is prioritizing preservation of its tariff advantage over other exporters to the United States, a day after Washington announced new tariffs on Canada.

events.title: Mexico's economy grows 1.7% in June, boosted by World Cup spending, INEGI estimates
events.why: INEGI's timely indicator points to a monthly pickup tied largely to World Cup-related consumption, even as industrial output stays weak and investment lags.

coverage.title: Mexico's economy grows 1.7% in June, boosted by World Cup spending, INEGI estimates
coverage.summary: INEGI's timely indicator points to a monthly pickup tied largely to World Cup-related consumption, even as industrial output stays weak and investment lags.

events.background: INEGI's IOAE indicator gives an early five-week estimate of monthly GDP activity ahead of the official IGAE data, after Mexico's economy contracted 0.6% quarterly in the first three months of 2026.
events.drivers: World Cup-related consumption lifted the June estimate to 1.7% annual growth from 1.6% in May, while industrial activity contracted 0.8% in the secondary sector in May.
events.implications: The pickup signals a partial recovery in activity heading into the second half of the year, but industrial weakness persists even as services strengthen.

events.title: Fuel theft network tied to Ruffo moved 800 million liters of gasoline in 15 months
events.why: Prosecutors say the scheme linked to former Baja California governor Ernesto Ruffo cost the treasury billions of pesos, one of the largest fuel-tax fraud cases to reach the federal attorney general's office.

coverage.title: Fuel theft network tied to Ruffo moved 800 million liters of gasoline in 15 months
coverage.summary: Prosecutors say the scheme linked to former Baja California governor Ernesto Ruffo cost the treasury billions of pesos, one of the largest fuel-tax fraud cases to reach the federal attorney general's office.

events.background: Huachicol fiscal refers to fuel-tax fraud schemes that under-declare imported fuel volumes to evade taxes, a long-running drain on Mexican public finances.
events.drivers: The investigation began after authorities seized 15 million liters of gasoline in 129 rail cars in Coahuila about a year ago, leading prosecutors to Ernesto Ruffo's customs company, Ingemar.

events.title: Grupo México profit jumps 90.9% in second quarter on copper prices
events.why: The mining group controlled by Germán Larrea posted net profit of over 2 billion dollars for the quarter, driven by higher copper prices and adding to its interest in rail infrastructure abroad.

coverage.title: Grupo México profit jumps 90.9% in second quarter on copper prices
coverage.summary: The mining group controlled by Germán Larrea posted net profit of over 2 billion dollars for the quarter, driven by higher copper prices and adding to its interest in rail infrastructure abroad.

events.background: Grupo México, controlled by Germán Larrea, is a mining conglomerate with copper operations and rail and transport interests across the region.
events.drivers: Higher global copper demand and a 56.7% cut in cash operating cost per pound of copper drove the profit increase.
events.implications: Total revenue also rose 34.9%, boosted by the company's rail and transport businesses.

events.title: América Móvil buys Peru's WOW to expand in Latin America
events.why: The Carlos Slim-controlled company agreed to acquire all shares of WOW from Liberty Latin America and Narvik Capital Partners, extending its fiber-optic network into Peru.

coverage.title: América Móvil buys Peru's WOW to expand in Latin America
coverage.summary: The Carlos Slim-controlled company agreed to acquire all shares of WOW from Liberty Latin America and Narvik Capital Partners, extending its fiber-optic network into Peru.

events.background: América Móvil, Carlos Slim's telecom group, already operates in Peru through a local subsidiary and is expanding fiber-optic infrastructure across Latin America.
events.drivers: The company reached a deal with Liberty Latin America and Narvik Capital Partners to buy all of WOW, a Peruvian fiber-optic operator, without disclosing the price.
events.next: The transaction's close depends on approval from Peru's competition authority, Indecopi.
events.implications: The deal came just ahead of América Móvil's second-quarter earnings report, with shares up 0.22% to 22.80 pesos after the announcement.

events.title: ATI Materials commits $80 million to new Chihuahua plant
events.why: The US materials producer will open a forged-products division in Chihuahua City, adding to a wave of manufacturing investment along the northern border.

coverage.title: ATI Materials commits $80 million to new Chihuahua plant
coverage.summary: The US materials producer will open a forged-products division in Chihuahua City, adding to a wave of manufacturing investment along the northern border.

events.drivers: ATI committed $80 million to open a forged-products division, ATI Forged Products, in Chihuahua City, announced jointly by Governor Maru Campos and CEO Kimberly Fields at the Farnborough International Airshow.
events.implications: The project adds advanced forging and manufacturing capacity to the northern border region's aerospace-linked industrial base.
events.background: Northern Mexico, including Chihuahua, is a hub for export manufacturing tied to US supply chains.

events.title: Ferrero to invest $86 million to expand Guanajuato plant
events.why: The investment will expand export capacity at a site that already ships about 40% of the company's regional production, as Ferrero aims to double its Mexico business within six years.

coverage.title: Ferrero to invest $86 million to expand Guanajuato plant
coverage.summary: The investment will expand export capacity at a site that already ships about 40% of the company's regional production, as Ferrero aims to double its Mexico business within six years.

events.background: Ferrero operates a confectionery manufacturing plant in Guanajuato that already exports a large share of its regional production as part of its broader Mexico operations.
